The fields carry input-shape validation from class-validator (@IsString, @IsNotEmpty, @IsBoolean) and API schema metadata from @nestjs/swagger (@ApiProperty). Describing the shape of input data and validating it is the normal job of an application-layer DTO. The file has no persistence, no transport handling (routes, request or response objects), no business rules and no domain logic. The swagger decorators are declarative metadata that sit close to presentation, but putting them on DTOs is standard NestJS practice, and they add no behavioral responsibility. They also do not move a domain or business concern into the wrong layer. No ADR prose was given that would say otherwise.
